rationale: Build on the current recurrent-tail/value-path float-reallocation baseline with a compact structural change instead of another scalar sweep. This edit keeps the same architecture and export path, but changes how the two reverse-tail recurrent blocks come online: the deepest recurrent block stays fully active, while earlier recurrent blocks ramp in later via a staged curriculum. The hypothesis is that under a 600s Mac-mini budget, concentrating early training on the strongest recurrent exit path improves short-run optimization and final int8+zlib behavior, then restores full recurrent depth later without adding compile churn or artifact bytes. The change is compact, compile-stable, and stays under the line cap.
title: Staged Reverse-Tail Recurrence Curriculum
